rationale: The human-factors meta-principle states that operators adapt to automation and interfaces and that human performance is part of the system. The new principle is a specific empirical instance: expert operators rate transparent automated assistance as at least as reliable as human assistance, while low-transparency automation is not rated more reliable. This specializes the broader human-factors principle to perceived reliability of assistance source and transparency in collaborative assembly.
